Definition: properly, a mesh (as allowing a liquid to run through), i.e. coarse loose cloth or sacking (used in mourning and for bagging); hence, a bag (for grain, etc.)
BiblicalUsage: When the text says saq, it means a mesh (as allowing a liquid to run through). In 1 Chronicles 21:16, we read, "…angel of the LORD stand between the earth…"; in 1 Kings 20:31, "…kings of the house of Israel merciful kings…". You hear it again in 2 Kings 6:30 — "…wall, and the people looked, and, behold, sackcloth…" — and in 2 Samuel 3:31, "…sackcloth, and mourn before Abner. And king David…".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe saq matters because God chose this word, and it tells the truth about how God deals with his people. I believe saq is still true for us, because the God who gave it has not changed his mind.
